goal_ko: 재실행·기록 경합·권한 오류 뒤에도 최초 실패 위치와 실행 불확실성을 잃지 않는지 확인했다. 과거 원인 확정이나 실제 모델 연결 성공 검증은 아니다.
reuse: Existing TrialRecord reader/writer OS lock, safe_io_failure, summarize_attempt, StructuredRuntime observer and first last_observation_error latch are reused. No second lock protocol, controller framework, model adapter or provider integration was added.

minimal_changes.change: TrialRecordError now retains the deepest existing project Python source file/line from the original exception. safe_controller_failure combines the safe operation/category/numeric OS codes with a fixed observation stage and summarized attempt. Absolute paths, error messages, filenames carried by exceptions, traceback text, locals, input and environment are not serialized.
minimal_changes.location_semantics: The last eligible project frame identifies the Python boundary; it is not claimed to be an underlying OS syscall location. Missing location or errno/winerror remains null.

minimal_changes.change: A record read failure followed by unlock failure retains the original read error and attaches a separate sanitized unlock failure, rather than replacing the primary error.
Incomplete or contradictory outcome=completed is summarized as unknown unless state=completed and one native start is observed. not_started without positive zero-start evidence also stays unknown.

Move observation reset after the poisoned-instance/room checks. Rejected replay previously reset the saved first failure and native launch state before raising runtime_outcome_unknown; it now preserves them. Deadlines, auth, launch flags, ACL and call limits are unchanged.

confirmed_synthetic_behaviors.result: Two separately spawned Python processes each perform 12 read/update cycles using the existing shared lock. Final revision is exactly 24, record remains reserved and no .pending remains. Readers open JSON only while holding the same lock; no overlapping uncoordinated replacement or lost update is accepted.

An owned read handle causes replace denial. The original JSON and failed .pending evidence remain. A subsequent update stops at write because .pending exists; it does not delete evidence, retry a model, mark completion or turn a missing count into zero.
Reading a dummy owned record fails with permission_denied. The independent safe controller report identifies operation=read and a project-relative code line; the unreadable attempt stays unknown.
Each reports its distinct operation, errno=13 and injected winerror=32, source file/line and unknown attempt. Secret sentinel message/path strings do not appear in serialized reports.
Injected Windows byte-lock denial is labeled lock with injected numeric winerror=33; record I/O is not entered and original bytes are preserved.
The primary read location survives; cleanup_failure separately records unlock and its relative source line.

The synthetic controller emits the safe primary report to its captured stderr before persisting it separately. A failed independent report replacement retains its own pending file; the already emitted primary read location and unknown outcome remain. Neither failure is swallowed or called success.

confirmed_synthetic_behaviors.case: native boundary before and after start
confirmed_synthetic_behaviors.result: With auth/preflight stubbed and only an exact base-Python sleep command permitted, actual OS child counts are respectively 0 and 1. The post-start observer fails before the older calls counter increments (calls=0), yet the live started state produces count=1 in the independently persisted report. All owned children have exited; no prompt is submitted.

A second runtime.run raises runtime_outcome_unknown without any additional native start. The original native state and first safe observation error remain byte-for-byte equal to their pre-replay values.

Injected private error messages, exception filenames, external/dynamic traceback filenames and arbitrary error attributes are excluded. Only existing project Python file/line, allowlisted stages, safe categories and numeric codes are retained.

safe_controller_integration_contract.historical_launchers: Frozen old launchers and all five historical records remain unchanged. No actual provider trial has adopted or run the new helper.
safe_controller_integration_contract.reader_and_writer: Controller read and worker update must both use TrialRecord for the same explicitly selected record and lock. Do not reopen the JSON directly.
safe_controller_integration_contract.first_error: Use runtime.last_observation_error[event] when available, rather than a cleanup stage that ran later. Keep the original caught TrialRecordError; its safe operation/location survive wrapping.
safe_controller_integration_contract.attempt_snapshot: If persistence failed after runtime start, pass the last in-memory native_launch_state in the attempt snapshot. A missing/unreadable snapshot is unknown. The old calls counter alone cannot prove no native creation.
failure_sequence: Emit json.dumps(report) to the owned controller stderr with flush=True before trying another file write. Do not print str(error), traceback text, locals or raw paths.
Persist the safe report through a distinct TrialRecord, not the record whose read/write/replace just failed. Re-read it to confirm durable publication.
If the independent sink fails, retain the already emitted primary report and its pending evidence, report the secondary safe error, and stop. Do not clear reservations or retry the runtime.
safe_controller_integration_contract.scope_limit: The report formatter does not itself persist or emit; the synthetic controller tests exercise this explicit caller sequence. A future actual controller must adopt it before a separately authorized trial. No guarantee is made if all output channels are unavailable or the process is killed before emitting any event.
safe_controller_integration_contract.launch_gap: Failure between OS process creation and supervisor.start return still has requested/unknown state unless separately observed. It must never be inferred as zero from calls=0. Existing runtime stages were retained rather than inventing unsupported precision.
